newsitem.title: USA: J.P.Morgan, American Century in partnership.
newsitem.headline: J.P.Morgan, American Century in partnership.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc said Wednesday it had agreed to buy a 45 percent stake in American Century Cos for about $900 million, and two companies will form a business partnership to pursue growth opportunities in asset management and personal financial services.
Two J.P. Morgan executives, Ramon de Oliveira and Edward Kelly III, will join American Century's board of directors.
J.P. Morgan said it will have certain management rights and an option to increase its equity interest in American Century.
James Stowers Jr, founder of American Century, and his family will retain voting control of the company.
J.P. Morgan said that through the deal, it will gain access to retail mutual fund distribution capabilities, products and technology that complement its core institutional investment focus.
American Century will diversify its fund offerings and its access to large institutional clients for defined contribution plans, it said.
J.P. Morgan said it expects the deal to close in four to six months.
The first joint intiative of the two firms will be to market defined-contribution pension plans to corporate plan sponsors, offering an array of mutual funds.
They also plan to pursue other opportunities to extend their reach in the personal financial services market, focusing on affluent individuals.
J.P. Morgan Chairman Douglas Warner III said the partnership will accelerate J.P. Morgan's asset management business by adding service and product expertise, distribution, and technology.
American Century, a no-load mutual fund company selling directly to individuals, manages $60 billion of assets in about 70 mutual funds.
Morgan manages $234 billion of assets, about 10 percent of which are mutual funds.
